around.headline: NCMC card and new BMTC 2.0 app now cover both Metro and bus tickets
around.summary: Commuters can now use the National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) directly for BMTC bus tickets, and CM Shivakumar has unveiled a 'Namma BMTC 2.0' app that books bus and metro tickets with live tracking on one platform, per TOI and Deccan Herald. Worth switching over if you regularly hop between metro and bus.

around.headline: Vande Bharat now covers Bengaluru-Mangaluru in just over 7 hours
around.summary: A new Vande Bharat Express run does the Bengaluru-Mangaluru route in just over seven hours, per The Hindu — a faster rail option if you're planning a coastal Karnataka trip.

around.headline: Nearly half of Bengaluru's sewage still goes untreated, polluting the Cauvery
around.summary: Karnataka minister Ramalinga Reddy said close to 50% of Bengaluru's sewage remains untreated, with a target of treating every drop only by December 2029; authorities separately warned apartments, houses and industries dumping into water bodies will face action, per Deccan Herald, TOI and The New Indian Express.
around.source: Deccan Herald, TOI, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Karnataka CM says civic body polls are being delayed by the ongoing voter-roll revision
around.summary: At the second Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) meeting, CM D.K. Shivakumar said civic polls are being held up by the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, per TOI Bengaluru — so don't expect a BBMP/GBA election date soon.

around.headline: Lokayukta opens a suo motu probe into Karnataka's school-shoe scheme
around.summary: The Karnataka Lokayukta has registered a suo motu complaint into an alleged scam in the state's free school-shoe distribution scheme, per TOI Bengaluru — a reminder that public welfare schemes are worth watching for procurement irregularities.

around.headline: A passenger's fight over a Rs 11 overcharge shows how to escalate railway vendor complaints
around.summary: A passenger had to push back hard just to recover Rs 11 overcharged by a railway platform vendor, per The Times of India — a reminder that even small overcharging is worth reporting to the Railway Protection Force helpline (139) rather than writing off.

around.headline: India hosts the BRICS summit as Xi Jinping and Putin arrive amid the Iran and Ukraine wars
around.summary: India is hosting the BRICS summit in New Delhi, with China confirming Xi Jinping's attendance and Vladimir Putin already arriving, even as the Iran and Ukraine wars test the bloc's unity; separately, Modi-Putin talks are focused on India securing critical minerals and rare earths from Russia, per Reuters, Hindustan Times and Moneycontrol — a deal here could matter for Bengaluru's electronics and EV-component makers who depend on these imports.

street_smart.title: You buy a mixer grinder from a Bengaluru electronics store. It stops working within 10 days, but the shop refuses a replacement or refund, pointing to a handwritten 'no returns once the box is opened' sign at the counter — echoing today's news of a passenger who had to escalate just to recover Rs 11 he was overcharged by a railway vendor. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Inspired by today's TOI Bengaluru story about a passenger who had to fight to get back Rs 11 overcharged by a railway platform vendor — a reminder that even small consumer disputes are worth escalating formally rather than accepting a seller's excuse. The scenario widens this into a bigger, common trap: shops citing invented 'store policy' to dodge statutory consumer rights. Consumer court basics hasn't come up as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The shop manager points to the handwritten sign and says there's 'nothing he can do' since you've already left the store with the box opened.

choices.text: Get the seller's refusal in writing (email or WhatsApp works), then file a free complaint with the National Consumer Helpline (call 1915 or use the UMANG app) or on the e-daakhil portal, citing the product's warranty and the Consumer Protection Act.
choices.feedback: Correct. A shop's handwritten 'no returns' sign has no legal standing over your statutory right to a working product under warranty — the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 overrides store policy, and both 1915 and e-daakhil.nic.in let you file for free without a lawyer.

choices.text: Accept the shop's explanation, since the sign was posted at the counter and you didn't ask about the return policy before buying, and pay to get the mixer repaired yourself.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A store can't opt out of consumer law by posting a sign — a defective product within its warranty period entitles you to free repair, replacement or refund from the seller or manufacturer, sign or no sign.

choices.text: Leave angry reviews on the store's Google listing and social media, hoping public pressure embarrasses them into fixing it.
choices.feedback: Risky. Public pressure sometimes works, but it isn't a legal remedy and gives the seller no formal deadline to respond — a written complaint through the consumer helpline creates a paper trail and a process they're required to answer.

choices.text: Go back and argue with the manager in person until they agree to help, since a firm stance usually gets faster results.
choices.feedback: Risky. It might work, but it can also turn into a shouting match with nothing in writing — if they still refuse, the formal complaint route above works whether or not you've already argued it out in person.

takeaways: National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or use the UMANG app for a free, quick complaint — most sellers respond once a formal complaint is logged.
For bigger disputes, e-daakhil.nic.in lets you file a case with the Consumer Commission online, no lawyer required.
A shop's own 'no returns' sign never overrides your statutory right to a working product within its warranty period — keep receipts and warranty cards as proof.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' in any form?
quiz.why: Article 14 guarantees equality before law, Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, and Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies — Article 17 specifically targets caste-based untouchability.

quiz.question: In India's monetary policy, what does the RBI's 'repo rate' refer to?
options: The interest rate the RBI pays on savings accounts
The rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The tax rate on stock market gains
The exchange rate between the rupee and the dollar
quiz.why: When the RBI cuts the repo rate, banks can borrow more cheaply and often pass on lower interest rates on loans; when it hikes the rate, borrowing gets costlier to help cool inflation.
